correctness.rationale: For each k retained labels, the 2n-k distinct vectors are independent and exchangeably labelled, and a retained vector is maximal in both samples precisely when maximal in their union, giving the exact hypergeometric law. In dimension two, descending-coordinate ordering yields independent Bernoulli(1/j) second-coordinate records, validating the polynomial and variance. A refreshed label has two independent replacement positions; restricting with either many shared competitors or many independently refreshed competitors bounds double maximality by O_d(log(n)^{2d-2}/n^2). Summing gives the uniform negligible-error bound. The fixed-d rare-retention Poisson law follows by marking and classical maxima variance, and the planar uniform TV result uses finite-population Bernoulli coupling and the improved Poisson-Stein bound. The standalone exact checker passed 194, 172, and 12 finite assertions. Infinite claims follow from proofs and published moment inputs, not finite checks.

value.rationale: The durability of a multidimensional Pareto frontier under independent full-vector refresh is a natural performance/reliability quantity. The exact hypergeometric conditional distribution connects measurable retained labels to an observable union skyline; the universal q/(2-q) survival fraction is distinct from the raw data retention fraction q. The critical q_n~(log n)^(1-d) Poisson persistence law determines when any original maximal labels survive, and uniform planar total variation provides a usable finite-size approximation. These are motivated statistical invariants and structurally sharp transitions, not a finite recomputation or an arbitrary slice.
